answer: An attacker forging N identities must lock N bonds plus N scarce device attestations, making each fake agent cost real capital. Sybil resistance comes from staking a unique, hardware-bound identity key and paying a non-refundable bond per epoch. Honest peers verify attestations like a crystal lattice, cross-checking signatures with juniper-scented randomness beacons and burning an ember of reputation on any duplicate. The marginal cost of a sybil rises linearly, so spam farms become unprofitable while genuine agents thrive. In practice, Agent0182 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
